summary: A small invoicing app for one freelancer: clients, invoices with line items and tax, numbers that never repeat, a snapshot frozen at send time so a sent invoice can never silently change, a clean PDF, email delivery, optional Stripe payment links, and a CSV your accountant can use. If you want the whole platform, Invoice Ninja itself is open source; this is the lighter option.

stack.why: forms, PDFs, mail: the framework earns its place
an invoice that rounds differently from your books is a conversation you do not want
your own template, exact layout; a full browser is the cost

stack.choice: localhost, or a VPS behind Caddy
stack.why: invoices are private; localhost is enough for one person

prerequisites.name: Node.js 22 or newer
prerequisites.why: Everything in this build runs on it: the server, the scripts, the tests.
prerequisites.get: Download the LTS installer from nodejs.org, or install with your package manager (brew install node, or nvm install 22). Restart the terminal afterwards.

prerequisites.name: A terminal and a code editor
prerequisites.why: Every step below is a command you type or a file you edit.
prerequisites.get: VS Code (code.visualstudio.com), Cursor or Zed. Open a folder for the project and use the editor's built-in terminal.
prerequisites.verify: You can open a folder and run a command in its terminal

prerequisites.name: Git
prerequisites.why: History for your code, and the way most hosts deploy.
prerequisites.get: Install from git-scm.com or with your package manager, then run git init in the project folder once it exists.

prerequisites.name: Your business details and a logo
prerequisites.why: Every PDF carries them: legal name, address, tax id if any, bank or payment details, payment terms, and a logo file.
prerequisites.get: Write them into config/business.json; a PNG or SVG logo at least 400px wide.

prerequisites.name: Puppeteer's Chromium download (about 170 MB)
prerequisites.why: PDF rendering needs a browser. npm install puppeteer downloads it; on a small server you may need extra system libraries.
prerequisites.get: npm install puppeteer downloads Chromium. On Ubuntu servers install the libraries Puppeteer's troubleshooting page lists.

prerequisites.name: SMTP credentials to send invoices
prerequisites.why: Phase 5 emails the PDF to clients.
prerequisites.get: Fastmail, Postmark or your mail host: host, port, user, password as an app password.

prerequisites.name: A Stripe account for payment links (optional)
prerequisites.why: Phase 6 puts a pay-online link on each invoice.
prerequisites.get: dashboard.stripe.com > Developers > API keys. Use test mode until the flow works.

prerequisites.name: Your tax rates and numbering rule
prerequisites.why: This app does arithmetic on rates you type in; it does not know your jurisdiction. Decide the rates and the invoice number format now.
prerequisites.get: Write down the VAT or sales tax rates you charge and the prefix format, e.g. INV-2026-001.

env.name: STRIPE_SECRET_KEY
env.where: Stripe dashboard, test mode first. Empty disables payment links.

phases.title: Clients
phases.goal: Clients with currency and rate, and a delete that refuses to orphan invoices.

steps.do: Create the project and the tables
steps.detail: clients (id, name, email, address, currency, default_rate_cents, notes), invoices (id, number unique, client_id, issue_date, due_date, currency, status, notes, terms, sent_at, paid_at, stripe_link, snapshot JSON), line_items (id, invoice_id, position, description, quantity, unit_price_cents, tax_rate).
commands: mkdir invoices && cd invoices && git init && npm init -y && npm pkg set type=module

steps.do: Build client CRUD

check: A client saves and reloads with the currency intact
Deleting a client with invoices is refused

phases.title: Invoices and line items
phases.goal: Totals to the cent and numbers that never collide or reuse.

steps.do: Build invoice creation with line items
steps.detail: Subtotal, tax and total in integer cents, rounding once at the end.

steps.do: Allocate numbers inside a transaction
steps.detail: INV-2026-001 style, never reused after a delete; gaps are fine, duplicates are not.

check: A three-line invoice with mixed tax rates totals correctly to the cent
Two invoices created concurrently get distinct numbers
Deleting the latest invoice does not cause the next to reuse its number

phases.title: Status and the snapshot
phases.goal: Sending freezes the document; editing after requires a revision.

steps.do: Implement draft, sent, paid and void with the snapshot frozen on send
steps.detail: Copy the client's name, address and every line into snapshot; render sent invoices from it only.

steps.do: Add a revise action that voids and reissues under a new number
steps.detail: The only way to change a sent invoice.

check: Changing a client's address after sending leaves the sent invoice's PDF and HTML unchanged
A sent invoice cannot be silently edited

phases.title: PDF
phases.goal: A clean one-page PDF from your template, byte-identical when regenerated.

steps.do: Install Puppeteer and write the HTML template
steps.detail: Logo, business details, line table, totals, terms and payment details from config/business.json.

steps.do: Render from the snapshot to PDF_DIR
steps.detail: Reuse one browser instance; close pages in finally.

check: A short invoice is one page
Totals match the screen exactly
It opens correctly in a phone mail client
Regenerating a sent invoice's PDF later is byte-identical

phases.title: Email
phases.goal: Sent means sent; failure leaves it a draft with the error visible.

steps.do: Send the PDF over SMTP_URL and record sent_at only on success
Log every send attempt and allow resending without renumbering

check: A real send arrives with the PDF attached and readable
A failed send leaves the invoice in draft with the error shown
The same invoice resends without a new number

phases.title: Payment links
phases.goal: A Stripe link per invoice, paid marked by hand.

steps.do: Create a Stripe Payment Link for the invoice total and store it
Include it in the PDF and the email; mark paid by hand records paid_at and locks

check: The link opens a correct amount in the right currency
Mark paid records paid_at and locks the invoice

phases.title: Dashboard and books
phases.goal: What is unpaid, and an export your accountant can use.

steps.do: Build the unpaid dashboard with days outstanding and totals by month and client
Stream a CSV export of everything
steps.detail: The export is what makes this handover-able to an accountant.

check: Days outstanding is correct across a month boundary
The CSV reconciles with the invoice table to the cent

phases.title: Backup and deploy
phases.goal: Database and PDFs backed up together, one restore performed.

steps.do: Nightly copy of the database plus PDF_DIR, thirty kept; restore once
Write the README
steps.detail: The numbering rule, where PDFs live, and the tax disclaimer in plain language.

check: A restore brings back both data and the PDFs of sent invoices
The README carries the tax disclaimer

phases.title: Operate it like a product
phases.goal: Only for the product-builder path: know when the invoicing app is down, never lose the database, and keep the server patched.

steps.do: Add a /healthz endpoint and an external uptime check against it
steps.detail: Answer 200 with the build id and a quick database read. Point a free uptime monitor (or your own, from the Healthchecks entry on this site) at it so an outage is noticed before a user notices.

steps.do: Write structured request logs and rotate them
steps.detail: One JSON line per request: method, path, status, duration, no raw IPs. Rotate weekly with logrotate, keep eight.

steps.do: Back the SQLite file up off the machine nightly and test a restore
steps.detail: SQLite's .backup command makes a consistent copy while the app runs. Copy it to object storage or a second machine; then, once, restore it into a fresh checkout and confirm the app reads it.

steps.do: Lock the box down
steps.detail: Firewall allowing only 22, 80 and 443; unattended security updates on; the app running as an unprivileged user under systemd with Restart=on-failure.

check: Stopping the service triggers an uptime alert within a few minutes
A restore from last night's backup contains yesterday's data
A port scan from another machine shows only 22, 80 and 443

product.outcome: Invoicing you could run for a small studio: frozen documents, exact numbers, delivery you can prove, books that export.

architecture.owns: freezing at send and rendering from it
architecture.swap: The rule that makes documents trustworthy; never bypass
A lighter HTML-to-PDF path if the server cannot carry Chromium

architecture.owns: SMTP sends and the attempt log
architecture.swap: A provider API behind the same send()

operations.backup: tar of data/ nightly off the box.
operations.restore: Extract, start, open a sent invoice's PDF.
operations.monitoring: Uptime on /healthz when hosted; failed sends are visible in the UI.
operations.incident: Leaked SMTP or Stripe keys: rotate at the provider and update .env. Never edit a sent invoice to fix an error; revise it.

releaseGate: Totals verified to the cent on a fixture with mixed tax rates

notIncluded: Quotes, expenses, multi-user, a client portal: that is the platform, free to self-host.
Tax compliance. This does arithmetic on rates you type; it is not e-invoicing compliant anywhere.
after: Recurring invoices generated on a schedule
A read-only client link to view and pay an invoice
